PC: Obtains history and physical examination with focus on allergic, cardiac and infectious symptoms.
Clarifies timing of pre-medication (e.g. diphenhydramine, acetaminophen, corticosteroids) and if other pre-medications such as ranitidine were given
Determines at what rituximab infusion IV rate symptoms started and if the iv has been clamped
Immediate review of airway/ breathing/ circulation with stabilization as required
Orders 50 mg IV diphenhydramine, 50 mg IV ranitidine, 1000 mg acetaminophen, corticosteroids IV (e.g. Hydrocortisone 50 mg)
Requests demerol 50 mg, identifies a suitable IV line and pushes the first 25 mg while watching the rigors dissipate.
If rigors persist after 30 seconds a second dose of demerol 25 mg is administered
Recommends that patient can resume rituximab infusion at reduced rate after period of recovery (e.g. after 30 minutes resume at 50 ml/ hour so long as vitals are stable)
MK: Identifies causes of low oxygen saturation including poor oximetry reading secondary to rigors and attempts to trouble shoot (e.g. moves oxygen probe, locates alternative oxygen monitor)
SBP: Clearly indicates to nursing when to be called again (i.e. any hypotension, hypoxia, fever, rigors)
Elicits help in managing the case from interprofessional team (e.g. nurses, supervising hematologist)
ICS: Provides reassurance to patient and coaches them with breathing
Maintains good eye contact with nurse embedded participants
Reflects back nurse embedded participant statements
Clarifies team goals and defines roles
Encourages input from nurse embedded participants
PROF: Respectful and responsive to feedback from nurse embedded participants
